title: Phase 9 · Stage 28: Filtering, paging and reports
summary: Give GET /books query parameters for filtering, sorting and paging with a generic PagedResult<T>, and serve the summary report as JSON.

steps.title: Never return everything
body: A real catalog has fifty thousand books. `GET /books` returning all of them is slow for the server, slow for the phone, and useless for a person. Collections are **filtered**, **sorted** and **paged** with query parameters, and the response says where you are:
Minimal APIs bind query parameters straight onto handler parameters; nullable ones are optional:
app.MapGet("/books", (string? genre, string? q, bool? available, string? sort, int? page, int? pageSize, Library library) => ...);
The envelope is one **generic** record for every list the API will ever page:
record PagedResult<T>(IReadOnlyList<T> Items, int Page, int PageSize, int Total);

Rules worth copying: page numbers start at 1; clamp the page size (here 1 to 50, default 10) so nobody can ask for a million; count `total` **before** `Skip`/`Take`; and reject nonsense (an unknown genre or sort) with a 400 rather than ignoring it.

steps.prompt: Paging arithmetic. What does this print?
steps.explain: Page 3 skips 10 items and takes what is left. `Math.Clamp` keeps a page size inside its limits.

options: It is always the catalog size
steps.explain: Clients use `total` to show *page 2 of 3*: it is the number of matches, not the size of this page or of the whole catalog.

steps.prompt: `GET /books?page=2&pageSize=2` with 5 matching books. What comes back?
steps.explain: Skip `(2 - 1) * 2 = 2`, take 2. `total` counts every match so clients can work out the number of pages.

steps.title: GET /books with query parameters, and /reports/summary
prompt: - `genre` (any case; unknown → 400 `ValidationProblem` key `genre` with the usual message), `q` (title or author contains, ignoring case), `available` (`true`: at least one copy in; `false`: none in),
- `sort`: `title`, `author` (then title) or `year` (then title), ordinal; none keeps catalog order; anything else → 400 key `sort`: `Sort by title, author or year.`,

2. `GET /reports/summary` answers `record SummaryDto(DateOnly Date, int Titles, int Copies, int OnLoan, int Overdue, decimal FinesOwed, List<GenreCount> ByGenre)` with `record GenreCount(string Genre, int Titles, int Copies)`, genres in enum order (only those with books). `Overdue` counts active loans past due.

// "a,b,c" from one property of every item in a JSON array, so one row checks which items came back, in order.
static string Keys(JsonElement json, string property) => json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array
static JsonElement At(JsonElement json, int index) =>
json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array && index < json.GetArrayLength() ? json[index] : default;
static JsonElement Get(JsonElement json, string property) =>
json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Object && json.TryGetProperty(property, out var value) ? value : default;
static async Task<JsonElement> GetJson(HttpClient http, string url) => await DojoWeb.Json(await http.GetAsync(url));
static string? First(JsonElement errors, string key) { var list = Get(errors, key); return list.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array && list.GetArrayLength() > 0 ? list[0].GetString() : null; }
hints: Start from `IEnumerable<Book> books = library.Books;` and narrow it one parameter at a time with `Where`. A bad genre returns `Results.ValidationProblem(new Dictionary<string, string[]> { ["genre"] = [...] })` straight away.
Sorting: `IEnumerable<Book>? sorted = sort?.ToLowerInvariant() switch { null => books, "title" => books.OrderBy(b => b.Title, StringComparer.Ordinal), ..., _ => null };` and a 400 when it is null.
Paging: `int size = Math.Clamp(pageSize ?? 10, 1, 50); int number = Math.Max(page ?? 1, 1); var all = sorted.ToList();` then `all.Skip((number - 1) * size).Take(size)`, and `total` is `all.Count`.
